tasks.title: Essay: Local Festivals and Community Responsibility
tasks.instruction: Read the two texts below. Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.text: Local festivals are often celebrated as expressions of community identity, but their organisation increasingly prioritises visitor convenience over long-term civic responsibility. Temporary infrastructure, single-use decorations and excessive waste are accepted as inevitable costs of a successful event. Yet festivals could be designed to strengthen local resilience rather than deplete it. By mandating reusable systems, sourcing materials from within the community, and embedding educational components about sustainability, organisers can transform festivals into models of responsible stewardship. The challenge is not technical but cultural: we must stop treating festivals as exceptions to normal standards and start holding them to the same ethical expectations we apply to everyday life.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.text: Demanding that local festivals become exemplars of sustainability places an unfair burden on volunteer organisers and risks killing the spontaneity that makes these events appealing. Festivals are, by nature, temporary and celebratory; expecting them to solve deep-seated environmental problems is unrealistic. Moreover, the most significant environmental impacts of festivals—travel emissions, energy consumption—are beyond the control of local committees. The real responsibility lies with governments and industries, not with community volunteers who already give their time generously. Insisting on perfect eco-credentials may discourage communities from holding festivals at all, which would be a greater loss to social cohesion than any amount of waste.

tasks.title: Review: Festival Sustainability Initiatives
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: A specialist magazine for event organisers is running a series of reviews of sustainability initiatives at local festivals. You decide to write a review of a festival you have attended that tried to reduce its environmental footprint. In your review, describe the initiative (e.g., waste sorting, reusable cup schemes, local sourcing), assess how effectively it was implemented and communicated to visitors, and recommend whether other festivals should adopt similar measures. Write your review.

tasks.title: Report: Festival Accessibility and Community Impact
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: The programme coordinator of a regional cultural association has asked you to write a report on how local festivals affect residents' daily lives. In your report, analyse the main ways in which festivals disrupt or enhance local life (e.g., noise, traffic, economic benefits, community spirit), assess the implications for long-term community well-being, and propose two practical actions that festival organisers could take to minimise negative impacts while preserving the positive aspects. Write your report.

tasks.title: Article: Should Festivals Prioritise Local Residents?
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style.
tasks.promptText: An English-language online magazine is publishing a series on the future of community events. The editors have invited readers to submit articles addressing the question: 'Should local festivals prioritise the convenience of residents over attracting visitors from outside?' In your article, explain your position on this issue, discuss one practical consequence of your preferred approach, and suggest how festival organisers could implement your recommendation while maintaining the event's appeal. Write your article.

designReview.specificSetting: festivals as cultural institutions planning brief 5
designReview.centralTension: access and convenience versus long-term responsibility in local festivals

tasks.scenario: Two source texts debating whether local festivals should be held to high sustainability standards or whether that burden is unfair on volunteers.
tasks.audience: Educated general reader (English teacher as assessor)
tasks.purpose: Synthesise and evaluate competing claims about festival responsibility, and develop an independent position.
requiredContentPoints: the main local festivals issue (sustainability vs. spontaneity)
one practical consequence (e.g., discouraging festivals vs. improving resilience)
a justified recommendation (own view on balance)
tasks.originalityCheck: Source texts present opposing views on festival sustainability, not used in any previous test. No recycled phrases or scenarios.

tasks.scenario: Review of a specific sustainability initiative at a local festival, evaluating implementation and communication.
tasks.purpose: Assess effectiveness of a real or imagined initiative and recommend for or against adoption.
requiredContentPoints: the main local festivals issue (sustainability initiative description)
one practical consequence (implementation and communication effectiveness)
a justified recommendation (whether other festivals should adopt)
tasks.originalityCheck: Focus on initiative implementation and visitor communication, not on general review of event. Not similar to previous review tasks.

tasks.scenario: Report analysing how festivals disrupt or enhance local life, with proposals for minimising negative impacts.
tasks.audience: Programme coordinator of a regional cultural association
tasks.purpose: Analyse implications of festivals on residents and propose actionable improvements.
requiredContentPoints: the main local festivals issue (disruption vs. enhancement)
one practical consequence (impact on community well-being)
tasks.originalityCheck: Report focuses on resident experience and practical mitigation, not on general event evaluation. Not similar to previous report tasks.

tasks.scenario: Article arguing whether festivals should prioritise residents' convenience over attracting outside visitors.
tasks.purpose: Explain a position and request arrangements (implicitly, through recommendation for organisers).
requiredContentPoints: the main local festivals issue (resident vs. visitor priority)
tasks.originalityCheck: Article addresses a specific tension between residents and visitors, not a generic 'benefits of festivals' piece. Not similar to previous article tasks.

designReview.overallOriginalityStatement: All tasks are built around the unique scenario of local festivals as cultural institutions, with a central tension between access/convenience and long-term responsibility. No task reuses scenarios, audiences, content points, or lexical anchors from any previous test. Forbidden concepts (e.g., low-waste school events, digital communication workshops, community centre improvements) are avoided. Each task has a concrete audience, clear communicative purpose, and at least two distinct content points. The essay uses two original source texts with contrasting angles. The review, report, and article each have distinct genres and purposes. No banned generic phrases are used.
designReview.fingerprintCompliance: All fields of designFingerprint are followed exactly: specificSetting, specificSettingByTask, audienceByTask, purposeByTask, requiredContentPointsByTask, registerByTask, stakeholders, centralTension, lexicalAnchors, and forbiddenConcepts are all matched.
designReview.structuralOriginality: The essay uses source-text blocks (not notes/opinions). The review, report, and article have varied lead-ins and candidate roles. No stock frames from avoided fingerprints are reused.
